minutes.headline: Committee heard three FY21 budget scenarios and held off choosing a target until the Monty Tech assessment is known
minutes.summary: The committee heard NEASC accreditation and mock trial presentations, then handled transfers, a lacrosse co-op and waivers, a batting cage donation, bag lunches at Town Meeting, and two trips. The superintendent presented FY21 budget scenarios after health insurance and Chapter 70 figures came in better than assumed. Members leaned toward waiting for the Monty Tech assessment before choosing a target, and the budget hearing date stayed open.

public_comment.topic: A teacher thanked the committee for honoring Judy Pierce, a longtime reading tutor.
A departing committee member read remarks saying she will not run for reelection and thanked the community.

what_happened.line: The committee heard three FY21 budget scenarios with different staffing levels and did not choose a target, with members leaning toward waiting for the Monty Tech assessment.
The superintendent said health insurance rose far less than the budgeted assumption and the governor's budget gave a Chapter 70 increase.
The committee voted to accept a budget update and approved three line item transfers, though the voice votes were not audible in the recording.
The committee accepted a lacrosse co-op with Fitchburg, JV waivers, and a baseball booster club donation of an indoor batting cage.
The committee allowed bag lunches in the auditorium during May Town Meeting and approved the student government and Philadelphia music trips.

why_it_matters: The FY21 school budget sets how much the schools ask taxpayers to fund, and the Monty Tech assessment is a mechanism that could free money for the schools or leave less available, so the target and staffing levels remain unsettled.
Residents who attend Town Meeting in May will be asked to vote on the school budget that comes out of these scenarios.
